subject: Optimize Toolkit: commitment tiers, caching credits, and quantization options
messages:
From: Sasha Green <sasha.green@vectra.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-07-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Optimize Toolkit inquiry - caching & quantization credits

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. We evaluated the onboarding deck and have two main questions before we commit to a pilot:

1) Pricing mechanics: our workload is very inference-heavy (real-time chat + embeddings). How do you typically structure a 12-month commit for the Optimize toolkit vs. pay-as-you-go? Specifically, what kind of percentage discount and/or credits do you apply for caching (prefix/KV) and batching improvements?

2) Quantization impact: our engineering team wants guidance on recommended quant levels (4-bit vs 8-bit) and how you surface accuracy/regression risk. Do you include quantization advisory in the commercial offer or is that a separate SOW?

Can you send a couple of concrete scenario price decks (one for a conservatively cached workload, one for an aggressive cache) plus the recommended commit bands? Procurement also wants any standard clauses that affect SLAs or credits.

— Sasha
Director of Platform Engineering
VectraAI

Hi Sasha — great questions. I put together two scenario sheets and a short proposal that map commit tiers to caching credits and include the quantization advisory we typically bundle for pilots. See attached: Optimize_Pricing_Scenarios.xlsx.

Quick high-level answers:
- Pricing structure: we offer tiered commit bands (Starter / Growth / Scale). Typical list discount on Optimize (toolkit + advisory) ranges from 10% (Starter) to ~22% (Scale) off list, with additional caching credits applied as a token-equivalent rebate.
- Caching credits: for chat-heavy prefix caching we convert expected token reduction into a one-time credit schedule for the first 6 months. The conservative scenario assumes a 15–20% token reduction; the aggressive scenario assumes 25–35%. Credits are applied as a percentage of committed usage (example in sheet).
- Quantization: for production we recommend an evaluation path: 4-bit (Q4) for encoder-heavy models with per-eval verification, 8-bit (Q8) where regression risk is higher. We include a 2-week quantization validation run with pilots at no additional cost in Growth/Scale bands; a formal SOW is only required for custom quant engineering beyond that scope.

Next steps: can we schedule a 30-minute call Tuesday to walk through the attached scenarios and align on the commit band you expect? If you prefer, we can surface an initial commercial term sheet and procurement-friendly clauses for SLAs and outage credits ahead of the call.

Notes: Attachment includes a simple mapping of commit bands to caching credits and an appendix explaining how we convert cache savings into token credits. Also included is an example rollback policy for quantized models in case of quality regressions.

Best,
Naomi Feldman

Team — forwarding Sasha's note and my quick reply. Key asks from Vectra: 12-month commit, caching credit mechanics, and built-in quant advisory. Procurement also wants standard SLA/credit language.

My proposal (for internal alignment before I send formal terms):
- Baseline commitment: $120k ARR (12-mo) as a starting anchor; commit bands in sheet scale from $60k–$500k ARR.
- Discounting: offer 18% off list at Growth band (middle band) with caching credits equal to 6% of committed tokens applied over first 6 months. For Scale band, 22% + caching credits at 10% of committed tokens.
- Quantization advisory: include 2-week quant validation + rollback policy at no charge for Growth/Scale. Anything requiring kernel work or custom quant pipelines is billable (SOW).
- Add-on: if they accept a private deployment pilot (VPC) we can offer an extra 2% concession or an equivalent one-time credit.
- SLA: standard 99.9% uptime target for hosted inference; for dedicated/private we can discuss higher SLOs. If Marcus can confirm whether we have room to waive the on-call fee for onboarding (one-time) that would help close.

Questions for you: can we stretch to 20% at Growth to accelerate signature if Vectra signs up within 10 business days? And Marcus — what is the maximum token-credit percentage we can commit to for caching in a public-hosted offering without large accounting headaches?

I want to keep the external pitch concrete but not over-commit — we should surface the spreadsheet and a short PDF proposal.

— Naomi

Subject: Optimize Toolkit - VectraAI pilot proposal and commit options (v1)

Hi Sasha / procurement team — thanks for the clarity. Attached is a concise pilot proposal (Optimize_Proposal_VectraAI_v1.pdf) and the scenario workbook. Highlights below so you have the key points up front: 

Summary offer (v1):
- Pilot scope: 3-month technical pilot + option to convert to 12-month commercial commit. Pilot includes: 2-week quant validation (Q4/Q8 pathing), caching configuration review, and batching/advisory sessions.
- Commercial options post-pilot: three commit bands (Starter / Growth / Scale). Example Growth band: 12-month commit = $120k ARR (billed monthly) with 18% discount off list and caching credits equal to 6% of committed usage applied as a token credit over the first 6 months. Scale band example: $360k ARR with 22% discount + 10% caching credits.
- Quantization: 2-week validation included for Growth/Scale. Any custom quant engineering beyond validation (kernel tuning, custom compilation) is separate SOW. Rollback policy: automatic fallback to non-quantized model for up to 48 hours on detection of quality regression above agreed thresholds.
- Private pilot concession: if Vectra opts for a VPC pilot we can add an extra 2% discount (or equivalent one-time credit) to the Growth band.
- SLA / credits: standard hosted SLA 99.9%; outage credits are described in the PDF. We are prepared to include procurement-friendly language around incident response times for pilots.

Requested next steps:
1) Please review the attached PDF and workbook.
2) Tell us which commit band you expect to aim for (Starter / Growth / Scale) so we can produce a clean term sheet.
3) If procurement wants redlines, we can produce a track-changes-friendly term sheet in DocuSign.

I can hop on a 30-minute call this week to walk through the numbers and the caching-credit mechanics. If you want more aggressive credits we can discuss a near-term signature incentive (sign within 10 business days) for an extra concession.

Thanks — looking forward to hearing which band you are leaning toward.

Best,
